h: Making a day of it at Beaulieu
p: Allow a good chunk of the day if you want to see everything the estate has to offer. The motor museum alone can easily fill a couple of hours for car fans, and once you add Palace House, the abbey ruins and the gardens, most families find a full day passes quickly.

Keep an eye out for the monorail, which glides around the estate and even passes through the roof of the museum building. It's a fun way to get your bearings and a favourite with kids who are starting to flag. Comfortable shoes are a must, because the estate is spread out and there's plenty of walking between the different parts.
If you're travelling with someone who isn't a car fan, don't worry. The gardens, the historic house and the abbey give everyone something to enjoy, so it's a good choice for mixed groups.

The surrounding New Forest is one of the best bits of a visit. Ponies, donkeys and cattle wander freely across the roads and heath, so drive slowly and don't feed them. Buckler's Hard, a historic shipbuilding village on the Beaulieu River, is a short drive away and makes a lovely follow-up, with a riverside walk and boat trips in season.

Exbury Gardens, known for its spectacular rhododendrons and azaleas in spring, is close by too, and the Georgian harbour town of Lymington is a short drive west for shops, cafés and boats on the Solent.
